resources.string: Shows when PhoneCast is capturing the screen

Enabled by default. PhoneCast temporarily uses minimum nonzero brightness while keeping the captured stream unchanged. With Modify system settings approval, casting also extends the screen timeout to about 24.8 days, even if dimming is off, and restores the original timeout afterward. Manual locking still ends capture. Force Stop may delay restoration until the next app start or reboot. If the optional PhoneCast Accessibility service is enabled, a physical touch temporarily restores brightness; otherwise use the restore action here or in the casting notification. Turning this off restores the previous brightness policy.
Enter the receiver address and pairing code, then approve screen capture to stream H.264 over your local network.

Optional notification forwarding sends brief cards only while casting. It is off by default. Message titles and text stay hidden unless you explicitly enable content. Package allow/block lists accept comma-separated Android package names. The current trusted-LAN connection is not encrypted.
Forward notifications to VR while casting
Include notification titles and message text (sensitive)

Injects only the taps, swipes, scrolls, and Back actions you request from your paired PhoneCast VR receiver. While casting with dimming enabled, it also observes the system touch-start signal to restore local brightness temporarily. It receives no touch coordinates and does not read app text or inspect window content.

Optional remote control uses Android Accessibility to inject taps, swipes, scrolls, and Back requested from the connected VR receiver. While casting with Dim phone enabled, the same service observes only Android\'s touch-start signal so a physical touch can restore brightness temporarily. It receives no touch coordinates and does not inspect app text or window content. Commands and video use the current unencrypted trusted-LAN connection.
Start PhoneCast with the saved receiver and pairing code
